title: INDEX(STR, SUB) returns 0 when SUB is not found — NOT -1 like most modern indexOf
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE FIND_DOT(STR, POS)
C     INDEX(STR, '.') returns the 1-based position of the first
C     occurrence, OR 0 if not present. Many engineers port this
C     directly to Java's String.indexOf which returns -1 -- the
C     downstream check 'POS > 0' silently breaks because
      IMPLICIT NONE
      CHARACTER*80 STR
      INTEGER      POS
      POS = INDEX(STR, '.')
      END
notes: INDEX returning 0 (not -1) is a tiny detail with huge port impact: every downstream 'IF POS > 0' must become 'POS != -1' in Java/C#. A literal port of the guard breaks for valid 'no-such-substring' inputs.
